capabilities.target: Executive's Drive documents, including board materials and draft financial results
Any email recipient, sent from the executive's mailbox
Executive's calendar; accepts invites and triggers document search and email prep

inputs.source: Calendar invite, free-text description, from any sender including outside the company

instructions.note: Instruction grants blanket authority to accept any invite and email a brief with document contents to attendees, with no restriction on which invites, which documents, or which recipients qualify.

The only oversight mechanism is a daily summary written after actions already occurred; no instruction requires verifying invite sender legitimacy, document sensitivity, or recipient trust before acting.
The instruction implicitly authorizes using the executive's full mailbox and drive access for any invite received, without distinguishing internal from external or trusted from untrusted senders.

elements.name: Inbound calendar invite from any sender
Executive's Drive (board materials, draft financial results)
Agent-authored daily summary used for executive review

controls.name: Daily summary review by the executive
controls.decay_rationale: The summary is authored by the same agent whose actions it reports; a more capable model can write more persuasive, selectively incomplete summaries (ASI09). Review also happens only after mail.send and drive_read have already executed, so it carries no preventive value.

controls.name: Human review gate for invites from unverified or external senders before auto-accept/prepare
Raw-action human approval before mail.send, required at minimum for external recipients
Least-privilege, context-scoped document access for calendar-triggered searches
Injection detection on free-text invite descriptions
controls.decay_rationale: A content classifier evaluates text, not intent; multi-step or obfuscated injected instructions in invite descriptions can evade it, and it does not scale with attacker sophistication.

controls.name: Independent, tamper-evident audit log of agent actions

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invite drives read of restricted documents and email to external attendees

attack_path.note: Untrusted invite with free-text description, from any sender including outside the company
Auto-accepts the invite and triggers preparation with no verification of sender or content
Searches and reads the executive's documents, including board materials and draft financial results
Emails a brief, potentially containing sensitive document content, to the invite's attendees, which can include the external sender who created the invite

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No control currently constrains this path, so it is already at the ceiling. Any new integration adding mailboxes, document sources, or delegated authority (data_scope_expansion), or a more capable underlying model (model_upgrade), would make the same unmitigated exfiltration path easier to exploit at scale.

evidence.observation: Anyone can send the executive a calendar invite; the invite description is free text written by the sender, providing an untrusted, attacker-controlled injection vector.

For each new invite, accept it if the time is free, then find related documents and email a short brief to the attendees -- chaining a read of internal/restricted documents directly to an external email send with no verification of invite content or recipients.
The executive's drive holds board materials and draft financial results, so the content read and potentially exfiltrated is highly sensitive.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step, so the brief can be sent to any attendee, including the external party who authored the triggering invite.
Act on invites as they arrive; the executive reviews a daily summary -- action occurs before any human review, and review happens only after the fact, and is written by the agent itself.

recommendations.action: Route calendar invites from senders outside the organization's verified domain to human review before calendar.accept_and_prepare runs; do not auto-accept or auto-prepare on unverified external invites.
Require raw-action human approval (showing actual recipient addresses and content preview) before mail.send executes, at minimum for any recipient outside the organization's domain.
Scope drive.search_and_read per meeting to documents explicitly shared with or referenced by the invite's attendees, rather than full search access to the executive's drive.
Treat calendar invite descriptions as untrusted content; pass them through an injection-detection classifier and strip actionable instructions before they influence tool selection or arguments.
Maintain a tamper-evident, independently generated audit log of every accept/read/send action (not authored by the agent itself) for executive review and incident response.

findings.title: Executive-directed email send of restricted/confidential documents lacks approval or scoping

attack_path.note: The executive's own trusted chat request
Reads documents, which may include board materials or draft financial results
Sends content to any recipient with no approval step or recipient restriction

forecast.watch_signal: A new agent-to-agent integration or chat relay capable of submitting requests attributed to the executive without strong authentication would let an attacker impersonate the executive, turning this trusted-source path into the same unmitigated critical path as F1. Watch for new accepts_tasks_from integrations or delegated chat channels.

evidence.observation: The agent manages the calendar and emails briefs with document content based on general instructions, with no distinction in controls between executive-initiated requests and invite-triggered actions.
mail.send has no recipient restrictions and no approval step for any instruction source, including the executive's own direct requests.
The drive contains board materials and draft financial results that could be included in an email with no confirmation step, even when requested directly by the executive.

recommendations.action: Require recipient- and sensitivity-aware approval before mail.send for confidential/restricted content, even when the request originates directly from the executive.
Apply least-privilege, time-boxed scoping to mail.send and drive.search_and_read credentials rather than persistent broad access.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how the agent process authenticates to drive.search_and_read, mail.send, or calendar.accept_and_prepare, or whether its own identity could be impersonated by another process.
The calendar system presumably records a sender address, but no artifact confirms that this is retained or used to verify authenticity before the invite is processed.

This is an inbound flow carrying attacker-authored content into the agent; it does not itself carry confidential data out of the trust boundary, which happens on the outbound mail flow covered separately.
No evidence that outbound mail volume from a single mailbox could independently exhaust a shared resource; the primary risk on this flow is disclosure, not availability.
No capability in this design writes to or modifies documents in the drive; cap.drive_read only reads, so tampering with stored content is out of scope here.
Artifacts do not specify drive API rate limits or quota behavior under repeated automated reads, so availability impact cannot be assessed.
Artifacts do not describe who besides the executive can access the daily summary store or how long it is retained.
A daily summary written once per day and read by one person is not a shared resource subject to denial of service in this design.

rating.rationale: The design implements a near-complete lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted calendar invites (free text, any sender) automatically trigger a read of restricted executive documents and an unrestricted external email send, with zero preventive controls -- no sender verification, no recipient restriction, no approval gate, and no credential scoping. The only control present, a daily summary, is detective, behavioral, written by the agent itself, and occurs only after the irreversible send, so it earns no residual credit (F1: critical/critical). The same unscoped, unapproved mail.send and drive.read are also reachable from the executive's own trusted requests with no safeguards, which is lower risk today (F2: high/high) but converges to the same critical path if any future integration lets another agent or channel submit requests attributed to the executive without strong authentication. Nothing in the design would resist a model upgrade or expanded data scope, because there is effectively no control left to decay.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in prompt.md and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; exact credential scopes for mail.send and drive.search_and_read are inferred from the runtime notes ('any recipient', 'the executive's documents'), so confidence on precise privilege boundaries is medium.

No information was provided on calendar invite sender verification practices (e.g., domain allowlisting at the calendar platform level); likelihood estimates for F1 assume the stated 'anyone can send' condition holds without additional out-of-band controls not mentioned in the artifacts.
